text:
Cole Caufield scored on a 4% chance in the first period, and he finished the night by ending it 54 seconds into overtime on a 35% look. That bookend is the cleanest summary of a game MTL controlled more than the 4-3 score suggests. The Canadiens produced 4.31 expected goals to BUF's 3.36, put up 67 shot attempts to 54, and won 64% of the simulated replays. They also took 36 of 57 faceoffs and gave the puck away 9 times to BUF's 19.

BUF opened the scoring when Josh Norris snapped one home at 8:21 of the first, but MTL answered twice in about two and a half minutes. Zachary Bolduc tipped in a power-play goal at 11:45, then Caufield made it 2-1 at 14:01. Alexandre Texier stretched the lead to 3-1 in the second, a period MTL won 2.02 to 1.41 in expected goals. Jack Quinn cut it back to one with a shorthanded goal at 9:52, a reminder that BUF stayed in this on opportunism rather than volume.

Tage Thompson tied it at 3-3 in the third, and the third period was the one stretch BUF won on chance quality, 1.05 to 0.85. Norris had the best look BUF got in overtime, a 29% chance that missed the net. Caufield did not miss. The two teams had already needed a shootout to settle things on Oct. 13, a 4-3 MTL win, and this one finished with the same score. Caufield, with two goals and five shots on goal, took first star, with Carrier (two assists) and Bolduc behind him.
